market_question: Will the Republicans win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: The Republican Party is the incumbent party entering 2028, having won the 2024 election. Historically, the incumbent party wins over 50% of the time, and the party's access to fundraising, the bully pulpit, and a built-in electoral base provides a structural advantage. While candidate quality and events matter, a 38.5% implied probability underestimates this edge. Given the long time horizon and uncertainty, a true probability of ~53% seems more accurate.
evidence_points: Historical incumbency advantage in US presidential elections
Republicans will hold the White House from 2025-2029, giving party infrastructure and donor networks a head start
The market-implied 38.5% is below typical baseline odds for an incumbent party
sources_consulted: Academic studies on incumbency advantage (e.g., Fair model)
Current political forecast aggregators (e.g., FiveThirtyEight if available)
